input: Draft a termination clause for my freelance contract

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Termination clauses can cover many sub-provisions — notice periods, termination for cause vs. convenience, payment on termination, IP ownership upon exit, non-disparagement — knowing which to include changes the clause substantially.
Whether the user is the freelancer or the client hiring one changes whose protections to prioritise — e.g., guaranteed payment vs. right to dismiss quickly.
The governing jurisdiction affects legally required notice periods, enforceability of clauses, and mandatory statutory rights that must be respected.
The type and duration of the project (short one-off vs. long retainer) determines how much notice is reasonable and whether kill fees or milestone-based payments apply.
The desired tone and strictness — e.g., heavily protective and formal vs. collaborative and flexible — shapes the language and how many safeguards are included.
Knowing whether this clause needs to be legally reviewed by a lawyer, or is just a working draft the user will self-use, determines the level of precision and caveat needed.
Whether this clause must slot into an existing contract (matching its style and numbering) or is being written from scratch affects formatting and integration.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a termination clause for freelance contract
gold.taskDescription: Write a termination clause suitable for the user's freelance contract, covering the conditions and process by which either party can end the agreement.

questions.title: Are you the freelancer or the client hiring one?
questions.description: Identify which party the user represents so protections can be prioritised accordingly — e.g., a freelancer needs payment guarantees on termination, while a client needs the right to dismiss for underperformance.

questions.title: Which country or state will govern this contract?
questions.description: Determine the jurisdiction so the clause respects local laws on notice periods, statutory rights, and enforceability.

questions.title: What type of project is this clause for?
questions.description: Understand whether this is a short one-off project, an ongoing retainer, or a long-term engagement, as this affects what notice periods and payment-on-exit terms are appropriate.

questions.title: Should termination be allowed without cause, or only for specific reasons?
questions.description: Clarify whether either party can exit freely with notice (termination for convenience) or only under defined conditions like breach or non-payment (termination for cause), or both.

questions.title: What notice period feels appropriate for ending the contract?
questions.description: Establish the user's expectation for how much advance notice should be required — e.g., 7 days, 14 days, 30 days — before termination takes effect.

questions.title: Should the tone be formal and protective or straightforward and flexible?
questions.description: Determine the drafting style — heavily protective legal language with multiple safeguards vs. plain, concise language that is easier for both parties to understand and agree to.

questions.title: Is this a standalone draft or must it fit into an existing contract?
questions.description: Find out whether the clause needs to match the style, numbering, and defined terms of an existing agreement, or is being created fresh from scratch.
